Enable settlement ambient chatter and extra residents
Covers towns, villages, ports, and lord halls. Disabling stops ambient bubbles and extra residents; it takes full effect after re-entering the scene.
0=off, 1=low, 2=standard, 3=high density. The tier adjusts chatter rates and extra residents across towns, villages, ports, and lord halls.
Uses the native resident count as the baseline. The standard target is about 2.0; high density can target up to 3x, limited by scene spawn points and safety caps.
Occasionally lets another nearby resident continue the previous line using local preset text without AI. Disabling reduces bubbles and scanning work.
Off by default. Ambient replies use AI only after you enter a separate endpoint and opt in; otherwise they use local preset text and consume 0 tokens.
Ambient AI API address (Base URL supported)
For example, https://api.openai.com/v1 or a full /v1/chat/completions URL. Only the address you enter is contacted; AnimusForge servers are not used.
Use your own API key. It is sent only to the local endpoint you configure; logs and usage notices never show the full key.
For example, gpt-4o-mini or deepseek-chat. Enter a model supported by the configured endpoint.

Sends one short test request. The test consumes a small number of tokens and shows an explicit in-game notice.
Ambient replies need only short sentences; 64-128 is recommended. Higher values increase potential per-request usage.
Only affects an existing multi-person reply event. It never makes AI scan or start events. 5-10 is recommended.
0 forbids ambient AI requests; 0-1 is recommended for low-end systems and 1-2 for mid-range systems. Local text is used after the cap is reached.
Estimated input plus output limit for ambient AI during this session. Local text is used after the limit; 0 forbids calls.
After each ambient AI reply, show estimated input/output tokens and the session total. Keeping this enabled is recommended.

After a formal duel, the winner gains the renown lost by the loser clan. No transfer occurs when both sides belong to the same clan or either side has no clan. Loser renown never falls below 0 and clan tier is not forcibly reduced.
Minimum renown lost by the loser clan each time. Default 20; if the clan has less, loss is capped at 0.
Calculates a percentage from the loser clan renown before settlement and uses the larger value with the minimum loss. Default: 3%.
Maximum clan renown lost in one duel. Default 150; 0 means no cap.

When enabled, equipment NPCs lose through gifts, trade, or post-battle loot is restored to its original slot after 3 days; existing replacement equipment is not overwritten. Disabling stops new and existing restoration jobs; re-enabling resumes registered jobs. Enabled by default.
Hold this key in a scene to preview and expand shout range; release it to open the speech input. Default: T.
Hold this key in a scene to preview and expand shout range; release it to open the complex interaction menu. Default: Y.
Press this key on the campaign map to open the AnimusForge terminal. Default: U.
During a scene taunt conflict, approach dropped coins after an NPC falls and press this key to collect them. Default: F.
Base shout range used when T/Y is pressed. Default: 4 m.
Maximum shout range while holding T/Y, capped at 150 m. Larger ranges show more preview markers.
Minimum length of a scene-shout reply. Default: 40.
Maximum length of a scene-shout reply. Default: 200; values below the minimum are corrected at runtime.
Minimum length of the parenthesized inner-thought section in scene-shout replies. Minimum 40; default 200.
When enabled, scene-shout requests no longer require inner-thought output and keep only the action and spoken-line format.
Sets the font size of text in scene-shout bubbles.
Extends the idle dismissal time for scene conversations based on visible player and NPC words in the current exchange. Default: 1 second per character.
How long the player must stare at one NPC before a passive reaction triggers. Default: 15 seconds.

When enabled, direct attacks on NPCs in peaceful scenes can trigger this mod scene conflict. When disabled, direct attacks return fully to native damage handling; dialogue arguments and taunts can still escalate conflict.
Affects only the shout input box. Default is transparent black; transparent white or pink are also available.
⚠️ Advanced debugging feature! When enabled, intercepts all UI clicks, state transitions, and low-level code stacks (Trace). Produces a very large log and is intended for developers only.
Adds a Developer data-management entry to the town menu for NPC histories, debts, and persona data; the character screen also exposes player history editing.
Generate persona and background for new adults
When enabled, the preprocessing API generates persona and history for hero children when they become adults. Existing persona or background is never overwritten.
Master logic-log switch. When disabled, Mod_Logic.txt is no longer written.
Enable only while investigating an issue. Writes detailed Mod_Logic diagnostics and may produce many lines in large campaigns.
Structured observability-log switch. When disabled, Observability.jsonl is no longer written.
Hit-rate statistics log switch. When disabled, HitRate_Stats.txt is no longer written.
Token statistics log switch. When disabled, Token_Stats.txt is no longer written.
Event-system weekly-report log switch. When disabled, Event_Logs.txt is no longer written.
Periodically clears current log files under AnimusForge/Logs by real time. Files and the UTF-8 BOM are retained. Default: every 3 days.
Every 30 seconds writes FPS, slow frames, and total frame time to Mod_Logic.txt. Tick/Scope timings are collected only with verbose logs enabled. Off by default.

Daily settlement registers maintenance jobs; memory overview, kingdom maintenance, and weekly-report preparation run later in bounded per-frame batches. Advances on campaign-map ticks and is not paused by travel. Enabled by default.
When deferred maintenance is enabled, work advances within this per-frame budget only when jobs are pending. Higher values finish faster but can create frame spikes. Default: 3.
Create thread dump when AI chat freezes

Only while AF free-conversation AI mode or scene shout is processing, creates a compact thread dump after five seconds without a main-thread heartbeat. Disabled for ordinary chat, non-AI play, and native saving. Enabled by default.
Maximum related knowledge entries supplied to AI per conversation. Terms are assigned independent slots by importance; later results fill unused slots. Default: 4.

Default CPU. GPU (CUDA) requires NVIDIA and optional CUDA runtime components; vector retrieval remains on CPU. Missing components, incompatible drivers, or GPU failure fall back to CPU. Restart the game fully after changing this value.

Maximum people, places, clans, and kingdoms injected into each AI request. Terms receive distinct entity slots by preprocessing importance; unused slots are filled only when the limit exceeds the term count. Default: 6.
Number of item, equipment, party, prisoner, asset, and policy candidates injected into AI. Fills to the limit when available; otherwise shows all. Default: 10.
Maximum ordinary chat-history lines carried directly in courier, free-conversation, and scene-shout requests before daily compression. AFEF facts do not count. Default: 100; range 10-500.
Daily summary target length is 1/N of the day's valid conversation characters. AFEF lines are excluded and never compressed. Default: 5; minimum summary length 80.
Maximum NPC/day-memory summaries per minute after a day changes. Default: 3; maximum 20.
Number of compressed-memory candidate blocks entering preprocessing. Default: 20; 15-20 is usually suitable. Rich-title semantic retrieval is used above this count.
Number of compressed memory blocks injected into the main chain. Default: 4; never exceeds the memory candidate limit.
Maximum additional rules supplied to AI per conversation. Recall and reranking counts are derived automatically and are not padded when highly relevant rules are insufficient. Default: 4.
When enabled, NPC parties with a clear need can pursue the player on the campaign map and start a conversation.
Allows Tier 0 players to trigger contact and is useful with high chance and short cooldowns. Off by default for normal play.
Applies when test mode is off. NPC contact does not trigger below this player clan tier.
Trigger probability scale for candidate NPCs. Default 35 for normal play; tests may use 100.
How often to scan nearby NPC parties with a need, in game hours. Default: 6.
After any proactive contact starts, no new contact starts during this many hours. Default: 24.
After an NPC contacts the player, it cannot return with the same need during this many days. Default: 14.
Maximum candidate distance equals player sight range multiplied by this value. Default: 1.0.
A food need can trigger when an NPC party has at most this many food days or is already starving. Default: 2 days.
A cash need can trigger when an NPC lord has less available cash than this value. Runtime respects the native party cash floor. Default: 5000.
A cash need can trigger when the lord can cover wages for at most this many days; 0 checks only cash and unpaid wages. Default: 2 days.
A troop shortage can trigger when current troops are below this percentage of party capacity. Default: 45; tests may use 90 or 100.
Prisoner overload or ransom contact can trigger at this percentage of capacity. Default: 90; above 100 triggers only when over capacity.
Low-morale contact can trigger at or below this value; 0 disables the need. Default: 35.
Mount shortage can trigger when mounts fall below this percentage of troop count; 0 disables the need. Default: 25.
Overburden contact can trigger when total party weight reaches this percentage of inventory capacity. Default: 92.
Clan financial pressure can trigger below this treasury value; 0 ignores the treasury. Default: 15000.
Clan financial pressure can trigger above this kingdom-debt value; 0 ignores debt. Default: 5000.
Inheritance or marriage-pressure contact can trigger when the NPC clan has no more than this many adult core members and at least one adult unmarried member. Default: 3.
Governance-concern contact can trigger when NPC clan fief loyalty is at or below this value; 0 ignores loyalty. Default: 35.
Governance-concern contact can trigger when NPC clan fief security is at or below this value; 0 ignores security. Default: 35.
Governance-concern contact can trigger when an NPC clan fief garrison is at or below this value; 0 ignores garrisons. Default: 80.
At or below this NPC clan influence, the ally count may trigger contact about a lack of allies; 0 ignores influence. Default: 40.
When the NPC clan has no more than this many friendly clans in the same kingdom with relations above 20, low influence or hostile relations may trigger contact about a lack of allies. Default: 1.
Multiplier for need-driven contact probability when the NPC already knows major events in the player history. Default: 2.0.
Multiplier converting effective player notoriety into additional proactive NPC contact probability. Default for normal play: 0.35.
Minimum need urgency required for proactive NPC contact. Test mode treats this as 0 at runtime. Default for normal play: 60.
After the player receives a request of a given type, greatly reduces that type trigger chance for this many game days. 0 disables type fatigue. Default: 10 days.
Multiplies both need-driven and notoriety-driven probabilities for requests under type fatigue, and reduces that need priority among candidates. Default: 0.20.

Candidate-weight and trigger-probability multiplier for mount-shortage or horse-purchase requests in map contact and unsolicited letters. Default: 0.35; 0 retains need detection but prevents proactive initiation. Map pursuit in test mode still uses 1.00.
Shared hard cooldown across map pursuit, unsolicited letters, and companion chat for romantic interactions with the opposite sex and private relations above 30. Default: 21 days.
Shared hard cooldown after an NPC with private relations above 20 pursues the player or sends an unsolicited greeting letter. Default: 42 days.

When the player is within player sight range times this multiplier of a kingdom settlement, that kingdom lords of a different culture who do not know the player history may proactively question their origins and purpose. Default: 3.0.
Shared hard cooldown after territorial questioning is successfully initiated. Default: 42 days.
Allows NPCs who know the player and have sufficient bond to send a real courier.
Raises chance to 100% and removes letter cooldowns; NPC knowledge, valid location, and a real motive are still required.
Minimum candidate score after averaging private relations and letter trust. Default: 10.
How often to scan unsolicited-letter candidates in game hours. Default: 24.
Per-scan chance equals bond score multiplied by this value. Default 0.25, or 25% at score 100.
After any NPC sends a letter, prevents a new unsolicited letter for this many game days. Default: 5.
Sender cooldown for NPCs with the minimum bond score. Default: 45 days.
Sender cooldown for NPCs with a score of 100. Default: 14 days.
After any channel talks with an NPC, wait at least this many game days before allowing an unsolicited letter. Default: 3.
Cap on positive or negative public-trust contribution to letter trust. Default: ±20.
Duration of reduced weight when the same NPC repeats a letter motive. Default: 30 days.
Weight multiplier for greeting, status, event, emotional, request, or diplomatic motives during fatigue. Default: 0.25.
Target body length for an unsolicited NPC letter. Default: 220 characters.
Logs candidate scores, chance, motives, cooldowns, and skip reasons to Mod_Logic.txt.

When enabled, scene shout includes only framed or manually invited characters; later bystanders are not added automatically. Takes effect on the next shout.
Weekly reports summarize world and kingdom events. Bulletins collect recent news after major events. Switching mode restarts collection and cancels old retries; existing archives are kept.

When enabled, executions, fief decisions, forced policies/wars/peace, raids, and similar events build discontent inside kingdoms. Opposition factions can petition the king, and rejected demands may escalate into a civil war (a temporary rebel kingdom and an actual war). Kingdom Stability and Rebellion must also be enabled.
Allow factions when the player is king

When enabled, kingdoms ruled by the player can also form opposition factions and deliver ultimatums. New ultimatums allow four weeks for a reply. Disabled by default. If player immunity to stability rebellions is enabled, these factions cannot escalate into civil war.
1 = roll by probability (each check is clamped to 5%–95%); 0 = decide directly from the expected value (it occurs when probability exceeds 50%). Default: 1.

A clan can lead an opposition faction only after its accumulated discontent reaches this value. Royal-aligned NPC clans that reach it after a negative event immediately withdraw support and become neutral; the king’s clan and the player’s clan are exempt. Default: 35.
How many weeks after a faction forms or a demand is rejected before another ultimatum is sent to the king. Default: 4.
Force an outcome when a civil war reaches this many weeks. Default: 12.
How many weeks after a faction is dissolved or a civil war ends before a new faction can form. Default: 8.

Maximum number of factions that can exist in one kingdom at the same time. Each has its own demands, discontent, ultimatums, and civil war. When one faction rises, the others enter cooldown and pause ultimatums. Default: 3.

Disabled (default): only one faction can rise at a time; the others pause until the civil war ends. Enabled: each faction can establish its own rebel kingdom and wage war against the royal house simultaneously.

The player clan’s strength must reach this percentage of the total strength of the kingdom’s established political clans to rise manually or propose a rising to a faction leader. 0 disables the strength gate; default: 20%. A player faction leader does not rise automatically, and refusing a dissolution order still requires this threshold.

A faction’s demands must be rejected by the king at least this many times before it can automatically escalate to civil war, including event-triggered escalation. A faction that has not risen after four refusals is dissolved, so the maximum is 4. Manual player uprisings are exempt. Default: 2.

When the global cap for civil-war factions currently fighting or waiting to establish a kingdom is reached, NPC factions pause their uprisings and resume when a slot opens. Player uprisings, approved proposals, and defiant uprisings are exempt from the cap but count toward it; registered coup wars also count, while starting a coup is not capped. Lowering the cap does not end existing wars. Native town rebellions are excluded. Default: 3 wars.
